content.user_title: Evaluate Scholarly Work with Structured Rubrics
content.value_statement: Research feedback can be inconsistent across papers, proposals, and reviews. This skill applies ScholarEval rubrics to produce structured, evidence-based assessments.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates research questions, literature review, methodology, data, analysis, results, writing, and citations.
Applies 5-point rubrics with qualitative evidence for each relevant dimension.
Produces strengths, weaknesses, critical issues, and prioritized recommendations.
Adapts evaluation depth for papers, proposals, dissertations, abstracts, and literature reviews.
Supports optional aggregate scoring through a local Python score calculator.
Uses the included evaluation framework reference for dimension criteria and checklists.
limitations: It does not replace expert peer review or discipline-specific judgment.
It cannot verify factual claims without source material supplied by the user.
The score calculator expects clean JSON score files and simple numeric inputs.
Schematic generation refers to a separate skill and script not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Review a Manuscript Draft
use_cases.description: Researchers can identify weak dimensions before journal or conference submission.

use_cases.title: Assess a Research Proposal
use_cases.description: Grant writers can test feasibility, methodology, impact, and evidence gaps before review.

use_cases.title: Teach Scholarly Quality Criteria
use_cases.description: Instructors can give students structured feedback on literature reviews, methods, and citations.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Paper Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this research paper using the ScholarEval dimensions. Summarize strengths, weaknesses, scores, and top revision priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Methodology
prompt_templates.prompt: Review only the methodology and research design sections. Assess rigor, feasibility, validity, ethics, and reproducibility.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Literature Reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these two literature reviews using ScholarEval criteria. Identify stronger coverage, synthesis, gap framing, and source quality.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Publication Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this manuscript for a target venue. Apply relevant ScholarEval dimensions, justify each score, and rank revisions by publication impact.

output_examples.input: A user submits an empirical research paper draft for comprehensive review.
output_examples.output: A dimension-by-dimension assessment with scores, evidence, strengths, weaknesses, and prioritized revisions.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether a proposal is ready for grant review.
output_examples.output: A readiness assessment covering problem significance, methodology, feasibility, impact, and the most urgent fixes.

output_examples.input: A user provides dimension scores and wants an aggregate evaluation summary.
output_examples.output: A weighted score summary with quality level, top strengths, weak dimensions, and recommended next steps.

best_practices: Provide the work type, target venue, development stage, and evaluation scope before requesting a review.
Ask for evidence-based comments tied to page numbers, sections, or claims.
Use scores as decision support, then review comments with domain experts.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the 5-point score as an objective acceptance decision.
Do not request broad criticism without providing the manuscript or key sections.
Do not ignore discipline-specific norms when interpreting rubric scores.

faq.question: What types of scholarly work can it evaluate?
faq.answer: It supports papers, proposals, literature reviews, dissertation chapters, abstracts, and other academic drafts.

faq.question: Does it replace peer review?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured preparation feedback, but expert reviewers remain necessary for publication decisions.

faq.question: Can it generate numeric scores?
faq.answer: Yes. It can apply 5-point dimension scores and can use the included calculator for aggregate scoring.

faq.question: Does it verify citations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can assess citation quality from supplied text, but it needs sources to verify citation accuracy.

faq.question: Can it focus on one section only?
faq.answer: Yes. Users can request targeted review of methods, analysis, writing, citations, or another dimension.

faq.question: What should users provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the draft, target venue, discipline, development stage, and any specific concerns or evaluation scope.
